subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should trusted inbound-decoration state be a canonical OpenClaw-owned metadata contract written by the inbound-decoration producer, rather than the proposed generic top-level message fields?
rationale: This determines the durable serialized ownership and provenance boundary across stored transcripts, imported histories, plugin-adjacent consumers, and future readers; it cannot be resolved safely by mechanical patch repair alone.

options.title: Adopt a host-owned metadata contract
options.body: Define one `__openclaw`-owned inbound-decoration record, populate it at the decoration owner, and update this PR to consume only that record.

options.title: Accept top-level fields as public contract
options.body: Explicitly document and support `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` as generic serialized message fields, including their import and provenance rules.

options.title: Pause this implementation
options.body: Keep the sentinel fallback and defer the new persistence contract until its owner and compatibility model are approved.

recommendation.title: Adopt a host-owned metadata contract
recommendation.body: Define one `__openclaw`-owned inbound-decoration record, populate it at the decoration owner, and update this PR to consume only that record.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied related-PR history shows direct work on the alternative contract boundary; confidence is limited because current-main ownership history could not be inspected in the read-only sandbox.
